REP stands for Research Experience Program, the undergraduate subject pool in the Psychology Department at The Ohio State University.

In this RMarkdown file, we prepared the raw data for analysis by performing exclusions (Qualtrics's built-in bot and fraud detection, finishing the survey too fast or too slow, skipping questions, answering inconsistently).

This file was copied from the file for cleaning the MTurk data and was edited by Mike DeKay in July 2023 and February and March 2024.

```{r, warning=F, include=F}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(rcompanion)
library(MASS)
library(gtools)
library(sjPlot)
library(sjlabelled)
library(sjmisc)
```

```{r, warning=F}
REP <- read_csv("REP_RawData.csv")
```

```{r, warning=F, include=F}
summary(REP$`Duration (in seconds)`)
dim(REP)
```

### Corrections on raw data
+ g2.1.2.2 = g.2.1.2.2;
+ Variable xl7.0.4.4 (with lower-case L) is not named properly in the data file;
+ Qualtrics assigned it the name QID353: xl7.0.4.4 = QID353;

### The block labels follow this pattern
+ g = gains, l = losses (lowercase L, but use L here because l looks like 1)
+ first number = cell (1-9 based on our design tables)
+ second number = option description order (1 = good first, 2 = bad first, 0 = not relevant)
+ third number = domain (1=disease, 2=invest, 3=wildfire, 4=drought)
+ fourth number = block number for similar blocks (repetitions that can be combined)

### Qualtrics Choice Coding
+ Program A (Sure):1 
+ Program B (Risky):2
+ Strong Preference for Program A:1
+ Moderate Preference for Program A:2
+ Slight Preference for Program A:3	
+ No Preference At All:4
+ Slight Preference for Program:5
+ Moderate Preference for Program B:6	
+ Strong Preference for Program B:7

### Choice Coding After Transformation
+ Sure = 0
+ Risky = 1
+ Rescored to -3 to 3, high favors Risky
+ Strong Preference for Program A (Sure): -3 
+ No Preference At All: 0
+ Strong Preference for Program B (Risky): 3

### Attribute Assignment
+ Domain Order is the order in which the 4 domains were presented to each subject.
+ Columns 1645 to 1713 contain strings of the domain order attribute formatted as "L6.1.2|L6.1.3|L6.1.4|L6.1.1".
+ We will extract these strings by finding their corresponding column number stored in column 1645 of each row.
```{r, warning=F}
# Preallocate 4 columns for the 4 domains in the order of which was presented to the subjects
REP$DomainOrder <- NA
REP$DomainOrder1 <- NA
REP$DomainOrder2 <- NA
REP$DomainOrder3 <- NA
REP$DomainOrder4 <- NA
REP$FirstDomain <- NA
REP$SecondDomain <- NA
REP$ThirdDomain <- NA
REP$FourthDomain <- NA
```

```{r}
# REP$FL_4_DO one or more R objects, to be converted to character vectors.
# If a value is specified for collapse, in our case, "_DO". The values in the result are then concatenated into a single string, with the elements being separated by the value of collapse.
# Ex: FL_50 - FL_50_DO, matches the column header
REP$FL_4_DO <- paste0(REP$FL_4_DO, "_DO")
```

```{r}
# Extract the number representing the domains from strings formatted as "L6.1.2|L6.1.3|L6.1.4|L6.1.1" 
# Referring to our coding scheme, it's the last digit of each block. Here is 2.3.4.1
for (i in 1:dim(REP)[1]){
  if(REP$FL_4_DO[i] != 'NA_DO'){
    REP$DomainOrder[i] <- REP[i,REP$FL_4_DO[i]]
    REP$DomainOrder1[i] <- substr(REP$DomainOrder[i], start = 6, stop = 6)
    REP$DomainOrder2[i] <- substr(REP$DomainOrder[i], start = 13, stop = 13)
    REP$DomainOrder3[i] <- substr(REP$DomainOrder[i], start = 20, stop = 20)
    REP$DomainOrder4[i] <- substr(REP$DomainOrder[i], start = 27, stop = 27)
  }
}
```

```{r}
# Assign actual domain name (e.g., disease) instead of numbers (e.g., 1)
for (i in 1:dim(REP)[1]){
  REP$FirstDomain[i] <- ifelse(REP$DomainOrder1[i] == 1, "Disease", ifelse(REP$DomainOrder1[i] == 2, "Invest", ifelse(REP$DomainOrder1[i] == 3, "Wildfire", ifelse(REP$DomainOrder1[i] == 4, "Drought", NA))))
  REP$SecondDomain[i] <- ifelse(REP$DomainOrder2[i] == 1, "Disease", ifelse(REP$DomainOrder2[i] == 2, "Invest", ifelse(REP$DomainOrder2[i] == 3, "Wildfire", ifelse(REP$DomainOrder2[i] == 4, "Drought", NA))))
  REP$ThirdDomain[i] <- ifelse(REP$DomainOrder3[i] == 1, "Disease", ifelse(REP$DomainOrder3[i] == 2, "Invest", ifelse(REP$DomainOrder3[i] == 3, "Wildfire", ifelse(REP$DomainOrder3[i] == 4, "Drought", NA))))
  REP$FourthDomain[i] <- ifelse(REP$DomainOrder4[i] == 1, "Disease", ifelse(REP$DomainOrder4[i] == 2, "Invest", ifelse(REP$DomainOrder4[i] == 3, "Wildfire", ifelse(REP$DomainOrder4[i] == 4, "Drought", NA))))
}
```

```{r}
# Get rid of column 1645 to 1713 
REP <- REP[,-(1645:1718)]
```

### Preallocate columns for choice and rating questions
```{r}
REP$Cell <- NA
REP$Order <- NA
REP$Original_Order <- NA
REP$Choice_Disease <- NA
REP$Choice_Invest <- NA
REP$Choice_Wildfire <- NA
REP$Choice_Drought <- NA
REP$Rate_Disease <- NA
REP$Rate_Invest <- NA
REP$Rate_Wildfire <- NA
REP$Rate_Drought <- NA
```

### We go through each row (subject) and extract their answers to the preallocated 8 choice/rating columns.
```{r, warning=F}
# To achieve a balanced number of answers at each level of our VDA variable (VDA [-2, 2]; 3 cells=0, 2 cells=-1, 2 cells=+1, 1 cell=-2, 1 cell=+2, a total of 9 cells in our apples-to-apples framework), subjects were randomized to one of the 18 cells with unequal probabilities. 

# To accomplish this, we had 2 blocks of questions of G1, 4 blocks of G2, 6 of G3, so on and so forth. With preallocation and other design, we have a total of 28 condition cells to check. 
for (i in 1:dim(REP)[1]){
  # One subject only gets one block of one condition cell. 
  # Because we are stacking the answers, two blocks (or more) of the same condition cell is checked at the same time.
  if (sum(REP$g1.0.1.1[i], REP$g1.0.2.1[i], REP$g1.0.3.1[i], REP$g1.0.4.1[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0 | sum(REP$g1.0.1.2[i], REP$g1.0.2.2[i], REP$g1.0.3.2[i], REP$g1.0.4.2[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0){
    # Between-subject
    REP$Cell[i] <- 'G1'
    REP$Order[i] <- 0
    REP$Original_Order[i] <- 0
    # Only one black contains answers
    # na.rm = T take care of missing values
    REP$Choice_Disease[i]  = max(REP$g1.0.1.1[i], REP$g1.0.1.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Invest[i]   = max(REP$g1.0.2.1[i], REP$g1.0.2.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$g1.0.3.1[i], REP$g1.0.3.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Drought[i]  = max(REP$g1.0.4.1[i], REP$g1.0.4.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1
    REP$Rate_Disease[i]  = max(REP$xg1.0.1.1[i], REP$xg1.0.1.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Invest[i]   = max(REP$xg1.0.2.1[i], REP$xg1.0.2.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$xg1.0.3.1[i], REP$xg1.0.3.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Drought[i]  = max(REP$xg1.0.4.1[i], REP$xg1.0.4.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
  }
  else if(sum(REP$g2.1.1.1[i], REP$g2.1.2.1[i], REP$g2.1.3.1[i], REP$g2.1.4.1[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0 | sum(REP$g2.1.1.2[i], REP$g2.1.2.2[i], REP$g2.1.3.2[i], REP$g2.1.4.2[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0){
    REP$Cell[i] <- 'G2'
    REP$Order[i] <- -0.5
    REP$Original_Order[i] <- 1
    REP$Choice_Disease[i]  = max(REP$g2.1.1.1[i], REP$g2.1.1.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Invest[i]   = max(REP$g2.1.2.1[i], REP$g2.1.2.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$g2.1.3.1[i], REP$g2.1.3.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Drought[i]  = max(REP$g2.1.4.1[i], REP$g2.1.4.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1
    REP$Rate_Disease[i]  = max(REP$xg2.1.1.1[i], REP$xg2.1.1.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Invest[i]   = max(REP$xg2.1.2.1[i], REP$xg2.1.2.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$xg2.1.3.1[i], REP$xg2.1.3.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Drought[i]  = max(REP$xg2.1.4.1[i], REP$xg2.1.4.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
  }
  else if(sum(REP$g2.2.1.1[i], REP$g2.2.2.1[i], REP$g2.2.3.1[i], REP$g2.2.4.1[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0 | sum(REP$g2.2.1.2[i], REP$g2.2.2.2[i], REP$g2.2.3.2[i], REP$g2.2.4.2[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0){
    REP$Cell[i] <- 'G2'
    REP$Order[i] <- 0.5
    REP$Original_Order[i] <- 2
    REP$Choice_Disease[i]  = max(REP$g2.2.1.1[i], REP$g2.2.1.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Invest[i]   = max(REP$g2.2.2.1[i], REP$g2.2.2.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$g2.2.3.1[i], REP$g2.2.3.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Drought[i]  = max(REP$g2.2.4.1[i], REP$g2.2.4.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1
    REP$Rate_Disease[i]  = max(REP$xg2.2.1.1[i], REP$xg2.2.1.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Invest[i]   = max(REP$xg2.2.2.1[i], REP$xg2.2.2.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$xg2.2.3.1[i], REP$xg2.2.3.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Drought[i]  = max(REP$xg2.2.4.1[i], REP$xg2.2.4.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
  }
  else if(sum(REP$g3.0.1.1[i], REP$g3.0.2.1[i], REP$g3.0.3.1[i], REP$g3.0.4.1[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0 | sum(REP$g3.0.1.2[i], REP$g3.0.2.2[i], REP$g3.0.3.2[i], REP$g3.0.4.2[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0 | sum(REP$g3.0.1.3[i], REP$g3.0.2.3[i], REP$g3.0.3.3[i], REP$g3.0.4.3[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0 | sum(REP$g3.0.1.4[i], REP$g3.0.2.4[i], REP$g3.0.3.4[i], REP$g3.0.4.4[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0 | sum(REP$g3.0.1.5[i], REP$g3.0.2.5[i], REP$g3.0.3.5[i], REP$g3.0.4.5[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0 | sum(REP$g3.0.1.6[i], REP$g3.0.2.6[i], REP$g3.0.3.6[i], REP$g3.0.4.6[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0){
    REP$Cell[i] <- 'G3'
    REP$Order[i] <- 0
    REP$Original_Order[i] <- 0
    REP$Choice_Disease[i]  = max(REP$g3.0.1.1[i], REP$g3.0.1.2[i], REP$g3.0.1.3[i], REP$g3.0.1.4[i], REP$g3.0.1.5[i], REP$g3.0.1.6[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Invest[i]   = max(REP$g3.0.2.1[i], REP$g3.0.2.2[i], REP$g3.0.2.3[i], REP$g3.0.2.4[i], REP$g3.0.2.5[i], REP$g3.0.2.6[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$g3.0.3.1[i], REP$g3.0.3.2[i], REP$g3.0.3.3[i], REP$g3.0.3.4[i], REP$g3.0.3.5[i], REP$g3.0.3.6[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Drought[i]  = max(REP$g3.0.4.1[i], REP$g3.0.4.2[i], REP$g3.0.4.3[i], REP$g3.0.4.4[i], REP$g3.0.4.5[i], REP$g3.0.4.6[i], na.rm = T) - 1
    REP$Rate_Disease[i]  = max(REP$xg3.0.1.1[i], REP$xg3.0.1.2[i], REP$xg3.0.1.3[i], REP$xg3.0.1.4[i], REP$xg3.0.1.5[i], REP$xg3.0.1.6[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Invest[i]   = max(REP$xg3.0.2.1[i], REP$xg3.0.2.2[i], REP$xg3.0.2.3[i], REP$xg3.0.2.4[i], REP$xg3.0.2.5[i], REP$xg3.0.2.6[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$xg3.0.3.1[i], REP$xg3.0.3.2[i], REP$xg3.0.3.3[i], REP$xg3.0.3.4[i], REP$xg3.0.3.5[i], REP$xg3.0.3.6[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Drought[i]  = max(REP$xg3.0.4.1[i], REP$xg3.0.4.2[i], REP$xg3.0.4.3[i], REP$xg3.0.4.4[i], REP$xg3.0.4.5[i], REP$xg3.0.4.6[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
  }
  else if(sum(REP$g4.1.1.1[i], REP$g4.1.2.1[i], REP$g4.1.3.1[i], REP$g4.1.4.1[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0 | sum(REP$g4.1.1.2[i], REP$g4.1.2.2[i], REP$g4.1.3.2[i], REP$g4.1.4.2[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0){
    REP$Cell[i] <- 'G4'
    REP$Order[i] <- 0.5
    REP$Original_Order[i] <- 1
    REP$Choice_Disease[i]  = max(REP$g4.1.1.1[i], REP$g4.1.1.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Invest[i]   = max(REP$g4.1.2.1[i], REP$g4.1.2.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$g4.1.3.1[i], REP$g4.1.3.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Drought[i]  = max(REP$g4.1.4.1[i], REP$g4.1.4.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1
    REP$Rate_Disease[i]  = max(REP$xg4.1.1.1[i], REP$xg4.1.1.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Invest[i]   = max(REP$xg4.1.2.1[i], REP$xg4.1.2.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$xg4.1.3.1[i], REP$xg4.1.3.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Drought[i]  = max(REP$xg4.1.4.1[i], REP$xg4.1.4.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
  }
  else if(sum(REP$g4.2.1.1[i], REP$g4.2.2.1[i], REP$g4.2.3.1[i], REP$g4.2.4.1[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0 | sum(REP$g4.2.1.2[i], REP$g4.2.2.2[i], REP$g4.2.3.2[i], REP$g4.2.4.2[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0){
    REP$Cell[i] <- 'G4'
    REP$Order[i] <- -0.5
    REP$Original_Order[i] <- 2
    REP$Choice_Disease[i]  = max(REP$g4.2.1.1[i], REP$g4.2.1.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Invest[i]   = max(REP$g4.2.2.1[i], REP$g4.2.2.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$g4.2.3.1[i], REP$g4.2.3.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Drought[i]  = max(REP$g4.2.4.1[i], REP$g4.2.4.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1
    REP$Rate_Disease[i]  = max(REP$xg4.2.1.1[i], REP$xg4.2.1.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Invest[i]   = max(REP$xg4.2.2.1[i], REP$xg4.2.2.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$xg4.2.3.1[i], REP$xg4.2.3.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Drought[i]  = max(REP$xg4.2.4.1[i], REP$xg4.2.4.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
  }
  else if (sum(REP$g5.1.1.1[i], REP$g5.1.2.1[i], REP$g5.1.3.1[i], REP$g5.1.4.1[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 1){
    REP$Cell[i] <- 'G5'
    REP$Order[i] <- 0
    REP$Original_Order[i] <- 1
    REP$Choice_Disease[i]  = REP$g5.1.1.1[i] - 1 
    REP$Choice_Invest[i]   = REP$g5.1.2.1[i] - 1 
    REP$Choice_Wildfire[i] = REP$g5.1.3.1[i] - 1 
    REP$Choice_Drought[i]  = REP$g5.1.4.1[i] - 1
    REP$Rate_Disease[i]  = REP$xg5.1.1.1[i] - 4 
    REP$Rate_Invest[i]   = REP$xg5.1.2.1[i] - 4 
    REP$Rate_Wildfire[i] = REP$xg5.1.3.1[i] - 4 
    REP$Rate_Drought[i]  = REP$xg5.1.4.1[i] - 4 
  }
  else if (sum(REP$g5.2.1.1[i], REP$g5.2.2.1[i], REP$g5.2.3.1[i], REP$g5.2.4.1[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 1){
    REP$Cell[i] <- 'G5'
    REP$Order[i] <- 0
    REP$Original_Order[i] <- 2
    REP$Choice_Disease[i]  = REP$g5.2.1.1[i] - 1 
    REP$Choice_Invest[i]   = REP$g5.2.2.1[i] - 1 
    REP$Choice_Wildfire[i] = REP$g5.2.3.1[i] - 1 
    REP$Choice_Drought[i]  = REP$g5.2.4.1[i] - 1
    REP$Rate_Disease[i]  = REP$xg5.2.1.1[i] - 4 
    REP$Rate_Invest[i]   = REP$xg5.2.2.1[i] - 4 
    REP$Rate_Wildfire[i] = REP$xg5.2.3.1[i] - 4 
    REP$Rate_Drought[i]  = REP$xg5.2.4.1[i] - 4 
  }
  else if(sum(REP$g6.1.1.1[i], REP$g6.1.2.1[i], REP$g6.1.3.1[i], REP$g6.1.4.1[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0 | sum(REP$g6.1.1.2[i], REP$g6.1.2.2[i], REP$g6.1.3.2[i], REP$g6.1.4.2[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0){
    REP$Cell[i] <- 'G6'
    REP$Order[i] <- 0.5
    REP$Original_Order[i] <- 1
    REP$Choice_Disease[i]  = max(REP$g6.1.1.1[i], REP$g6.1.1.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Invest[i]   = max(REP$g6.1.2.1[i], REP$g6.1.2.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$g6.1.3.1[i], REP$g6.1.3.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1 
    REP$Choice_Drought[i]  = max(REP$g6.1.4.1[i], REP$g6.1.4.2[i], na.rm = T) - 1
    REP$Rate_Disease[i]  = max(REP$xg6.1.1.1[i], REP$xg6.1.1.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Invest[i]   = max(REP$xg6.1.2.1[i], REP$xg6.1.2.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Wildfire[i] = max(REP$xg6.1.3.1[i], REP$xg6.1.3.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
    REP$Rate_Drought[i]  = max(REP$xg6.1.4.1[i], REP$xg6.1.4.2[i], na.rm = T) - 4 
  }
  else if(sum(REP$g6.2.1.1[i], REP$g6.2.2.1[i], REP$g6.2.3.1[i], REP$g6.2.4.1[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0 | sum(REP$g6.2.1.2[i], REP$g6.2.2.2[i], REP$g6.2.3.2[i], REP$g6.2.4.2[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 0){
    REP$Cell[i] <- 'G6'
    REP$Order[i] <- -0.5

  else if (sum(REP$l5.2.1.1[i], REP$l5.2.2.1[i], REP$l5.2.3.1[i], REP$l5.2.4.1[i], na.rm = TRUE) > 1){
```

### Data Cleaning

Data Cleaning Step 1

### Exclude subjects with 0 questions answered.
```{r,echo=F,warning=F}

list

REPNew[rowSums(is.na(REPNew[,21:28])) == ncol(REPNew[,21:28]), 21:28]
```

### 20 rows (38 118 125 144 148 185 274 302 303 323 446 471 496 498 593 608 663 669 670 671) were excluded. These "subjects" never engaged with the survey are not considered to have been successfully recruited. They are not counted in our initial sample size.

Data Cleaning Step 2

### Qualtrics built-in checks
### RecapchaScore excluded 1, so n = 650.
### RelevantIDDuplicateScore exluded 80, so n = 570.
### RelevantFraudIDScore excluded 6, so n = 564.
```{r, include = F}
REPNew[is.na(REPNew$Q_RecaptchaScore),c(11,35,6,21:28)]
# Pay extra attention to the NAs, physically check the rows before excluding them
REPNew[(REPNew$Q_RecaptchaScore < 0.5 & !is.na(REPNew$Q_RecaptchaScore)),c(11,35,6,21:28)]
REPNew[(REPNew$Q_RelevantIDDuplicateScore >= 75 & !is.na(REPNew$Q_RelevantIDDuplicateScore)),c(11,35,6,21:28)]
REPNew[(REPNew$Q_RelevantIDFraudScore >= 30 & !is.na(REPNew$Q_RelevantIDFraudScore)),c(11,35,6,21:28)]
```

```{r}
# remove duplicates

dim(REPNew)[1]
```

Data Cleaning Step 3

### Delete subjects who finished in more than 2.5 SDs above or below the mean completion time, after normalization.
### Because the original duration variable was positively skewed, I used the Box-Cox transformation.
```{r, echo=FALSE}
names(REPNew)[names(REPNew) == 'Duration (in seconds)'] = 'Duration'
plotNormalHistogram(REPNew$Duration)
qqnorm(REPNew$Duration, ylab = "Duration")
qqline(REPNew$Duration, col = "red")

Box = boxcox(REPNew$Duration ~ 1, lambda = seq(-3,3))
lambda = Box$x[which(Box$y == max(Box$y))]
# lambda  
# -0.3939394

REPNew$t_duration = (REPNew$Duration^lambda - 1)/lambda
plotNormalHistogram(REPNew$t_duration)

mean_d <- mean(REPNew$t_duration)
# mean_d
# 2.221161

sd_d <- sd(REPNew$t_duration)
# sd_d
# 0.08378852

low_dura <- mean_d - 2.5*sd_d
# low_dura 
# 2.5sd, 2.01169
high_dura <- mean_d + 2.5*sd_d
# high_dura
# 2.5sd, 2.430632
```

```{r, include=F}
# Inverse transformation of box-cox coefficients to duration (in seconds) to check the cutoffs
DurationMin = (lambda*low_dura + 1)^(1/(lambda))
DurationMax = (lambda*high_dura + 1)^(1/(lambda))
DurationMin
DurationMax
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
# Similarly, double check the excluded rows
dim(REPNew[REPNew$Duration < DurationMin, c(6,19:28)])[1]
REPNew[REPNew$Duration < DurationMin, c(6,19:28)]
dim(REPNew[REPNew$Duration > DurationMax, c(6,19:28)])[1]
REPNew[REPNew$Duration > DurationMax, c(6,19:28)]
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
# Less accurate way to find the 2.5 std cutoffs: quantiles. 
duration = REPNew$Duration    
quantile(duration, c(0.0062,0.9938)) 
```

### The lower cutoff excluded 8, so n = 556.
### The upper cutoff excluded 6, so n = 548.
```{r,echo=FALSE}
dim(REPNew)
# less than 2.5sd: 8 excluded
REPNew <- REPNew[which(REPNew$t_duration >= low_dura), ]
dim(REPNew)
# more than 2.5sd: 6 excluded
REPNew <- REPNew[which(REPNew$t_duration <= high_dura), ]
dim(REPNew)
```

Data Cleaning Step 5

### Exclude if two or more of the eight choice/rating questions are not answered.

Data Cleaning Step 6

### Exclude if one or more of the choice/rating pairs do not match.

Revisit numerical coding scheme of choice and rating answers.

Qualtrics built-in Coding scheme

+ Program A (Sure):1 
+ Program B (Risky):2
+ Strong Preference for Program A:1
+ Moderate Preference for Program A:2
+ Slight Preference for Program A:3	
+ No Preference At All:4
+ Slight Preference for Program:5
+ Moderate Preference for Program B:6	
+ Strong Preference for Program B:7

Recoded Values

+ Sure = 0
+ Risky = 1
+ Rescored to -3 to 3, high favors Risky
+ Strong Preference for Program A (Sure): -3 
+ No Preference At All: 0
+ Strong Preference for Program B (Risky): 3

```{r,echo=FALSE}
## We want to remove rows with count >= 2, meaning the participant didn't answer 2 or more answers.
## We also want to remove rows where check is != 0 since we don't want any inconsistency between choice and rating (slacking off).
## Do we consider a missing answer paired with an answer as inconsistency? No!
## column 22 is Choice_Disease

REPNew$Check <- 0
REPNew$Count <- 0

for (i in 1:dim(REPNew)[1]){
  for(j in 0:3){
    # Only if choose option A = 0, rating question answers ranged in (0,3], is inconsistency
    # Only if choose option B = 1, rating question answers ranged in [-3,0), is inconsistency
    if((REPNew[i,21+j] == 0 && REPNew[i,25+j] > 0)
       | (REPNew[i,21+j] == 1 && REPNew[i,25+j] < 0 && REPNew[i,25+j] >= -3)){
      REPNew$Check[i] <- REPNew$Check[i] + 1
    }
    else{
      REPNew$Check[i] <- REPNew$Check[i] + 0
    }
    # checking if one of the binary choice is not answered
    if(REPNew[i,21+j] < 0){
      REPNew$Count[i] <- REPNew$Count[i] + 1
    }
    else{
      REPNew$Count[i] <- REPNew$Count[i] + 0
    }
    # checking if one of the rating choice is not answered
    if(REPNew[i,25+j] < -3){
      REPNew$Count[i] <- REPNew$Count[i] + 1
    }
    else{
      REPNew$Count[i] <- REPNew$Count[i] + 0
    }
  }
}
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
dim(REPNew)
sublist1 <- REPNew[which(REPNew$Count >= 2),c(35,5,21:28)]
sublist2 <- REPNew[which(REPNew$Check > 0),c(35,5,21:28)]
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
REPNew[REPNew$ID==702,c(35,5,21:28)]
REPNew[REPNew$ID==1006,c(35,5,21:28)]
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
which(REPNew$Count >= 2)
which(REPNew$Check > 0)
list <- c(which(REPNew$Count >= 2), which(REPNew$Check > 0))
```

*RUN ONLY ONCE*

### The two exclusions above were applied simultaneously, but we treat them as if the missing value check was applied first. If a subject is in the first exlusion list, they are removed. If they are also in the second exclusion list, the second exclusion would not matter (but this did not happen here). What matters is the final n after both exclusions.

### Before these exclusions, n = 546.
### The missing value check excluded 2, so n = 544.
### The inconsistency check excluded an additional 23, so n = 521.
```{r,echo=FALSE}
# Check their answers, combine the list of sloppy participants to REMOVE duplicates.
# Because only we exclude participants with one exclusion criteria, their row number will be updated!
# Can also use ID to form exclusion list to be extra cautious.
REPNew[list, c(35,21:28)]
sort(list)
newlist <- unique(list)
newlist
```

### 521 subjects left after final check
```{r,echo=FALSE}
REPNew <- REPNew[-list, ]
dim(REPNew)
```

---------------------------------------- Subject Exclusion Process Completed.---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Some Final Preparations

+ Create variables for Frame and VDA (ValenceDiff).
```{r,echo=FALSE}
for (i in 1:dim(REPNew)[1]){
  # Attribute "Cell" in REPNew contains information on frame & cell number
  # Ex: G6
  if(str_contains(REPNew$Cell[i],'G')){
    REPNew$Frame[i] = 'Gain'
  }else if(str_contains(REPNew$Cell[i],'L')){
    REPNew$Frame[i] = 'Loss'
  }else{
    REPNew$Frame[i] = NA
  }
  # 5 levels of VDA for 9 cells
  if(str_contains(REPNew$Cell[i],1) | str_contains(REPNew$Cell[i],5) | str_contains(REPNew$Cell[i],9)){
    REPNew$VDA[i] = 0
  }else if(str_contains(REPNew$Cell[i],2) | str_contains(REPNew$Cell[i],6)){
    REPNew$VDA[i] = 1
  }else if(str_contains(REPNew$Cell[i],4) | str_contains(REPNew$Cell[i],8)){
    REPNew$VDA[i] = -1
  }else if(str_contains(REPNew$Cell[i],3)){
    REPNew$VDA[i] = 2
  }else if(str_contains(REPNew$Cell[i],7)){
    REPNew$VDA[i] = -2
  }else{
    REPNew$VDA[i] = NA
  }
}
```

+ Sort data by Cell and see the number of subjects per cell.
```{r,echo=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
set.seed(1)
REPNew %>% 
  group_by(Cell) %>%
  summarise(num_rows = length(Cell))
```

+ Transform the dataset from wide to tall (4 rows per subject).
```{r,echo=FALSE}
# Transforming previous wide dataset with 4 columns representing choices to 1 column, with an additional column specifying the domain each answer is in.
tallREP <- REPNew %>% pivot_longer(c(21:28), names_to =  c(".value", "Domain"), names_sep = "_")
```

+ Keep only the relevant variables.
```{r,echo=F}
smallREP <- tallREP[,15:36]
dim(smallREP)[1]
```

+ Create contrast codes for Frame.
```{r,echo=F}
# Transform the frame attribute such that gain frame has a value of -0.5 and loss frame has a value of 0.5
smallREP$Frame <- ifelse(smallREP$Frame == "Gain", -0.5, 0.5)
smallREP$Frame <- as.factor(smallREP$Frame)
```

+ Save the tall datafile for analysis.
```{r,echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
write.csv(smallREP, "REP_CleanData.csv")
```
